ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an 8-pin timer chip, with pin numbers including 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and the layout conforms to a 555 timer. Pin 8 and pin 4 are connected to the upper power supply line, pin 1 is grounded, pin 3 is the output terminal on the right, and pin 5 is grounded through a capacitor. On the left there is a timing network composed of R1, adjustable resistor R3, R2, diode VD, and capacitor C; the node of capacitor C is connected near pins 2 and 6, and pin 7 is connected into the charging and discharging path composed of R3, VD, etc. Reasoning: In a 555 oscillation circuit, timing capacitor C charges and discharges through the external resistor network, and the charging time and discharging time determine the duration of the high level and low level at output terminal pin 3. Adjusting R3 will change the resistance ratio in the charging and discharging paths, thereby changing the relative relationship between the high-level time and the low-level time, rather than mainly changing the output amplitude. Therefore adjusting R3 is adjusting the duty cycle parameter of the circuit output pulse.
